basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 21.' and it opens '| Vers. 21. Reducetque vos ad terram patrum vestrorum. Magno desiderio patriarcha Jacob'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: | Vers. 21. Reducetque vos ad terram patrum vestrorum. Magno desiderio patriarcha Jacob tenebatur, cupiens in ea terra sepeliri, ubi passurum Christum noverat et redimendum genus humanum. Denique, ut ferunt periti sanctorum locorum, ab eo loco qui Abramium dicitur, ubi Abraham et Isaac sepulti sunt, usque ad locum Dominicae passionis, triginta fere millia passuum habentur, ut ipso quoque numero qui in T littera continetur, mysterium Dominicae passionis ostendatur.
